body_markdown:
Volkswagen resurrected the Scout nameplate and turned it into a standalone brand[in 2024](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/scout-motors-unveils-2027-terra-pickup-and-traveler-suv/) . The company’s first models aren’t due out until 2028, though, so it’s whetting our appetite with two concepts called Scout Traveler Mountainside and Scout Traveler Trail-Ready.


Both design studies are evolutions of the close-to-production Traveler concept, which was introduced two years ago. Designed with an emphasis on luxury, the Mountainside (pictured below) is finished in a new shade of dark brown called Morning Dusk with a contrasting brown and gray interior called Alpine District. It’s an attractive, outdoorsy color combination that works well on the Traveler, and it’s inspired by the company’s heritage: Woven cloth was available on[some of the original Scout models](https://www.hagerty.com/media/buying-and-selling/2020-hagerty-bull-market-selection-1971-80-international-harvester-scout/) .


Several features set the Mountainside apart from the Traveler shown in 2024, such as 22-inch Vault wheels that almost look rally-inspired, a panoramic sunroof, and recycled walnut interior trim. Houndstooth upholstery on the headliner adds another retro-styled touch.

As its name implies, the Traveler Trail-Ready (pictured below) explores the more rugged side of the SUV. It’s finished in Galvanized Steel with a contrasting Canvas-colored roof, and it’s decked out with off-road-ready parts. The list includes metal bumpers on both ends, rock rails, 18-inch beadlock wheels wrapped by 35-inch off-road tires, and a rear-mounted spare wheel carrier with an integrated fuel can. We haven’t seen interior photos yet, but Scout claims that the Denim District theme is inspired by “durable American workwear” and Scout’s agricultural roots (the original Scout was designed and built by International Harvester).


The new Scout Traveler Mountainside and Scout Traveler Trail-Ready concepts will be presented to the public on September 4, 2026, during the Jazz Aspen Snowmass Labor Day Experience in Aspen, Colorado. Neither has been confirmed for production yet, but we wouldn’t be surprised if they preview some of the regular-production model’s available option packages and accessories.


Speaking of the regular-production model, Scout tells us that it’s still on track to deliver the first examples to customers[in 2028](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/rumor-of-scout-motors-production-delays-may-be-just-that/) . The SUV will be built in a new factory located in Blythewood, South Carolina, and it will be sold alongside the Terra pickup.
